On Fri, Nov 5, 2027 at 08:18, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating immediately to runtime engineering and our on-call infra folks.

I've started a quick triage. Early indicators from the pcap and our ingress metrics: 3 observations

1) We see chunked responses being transmitted from the model backend at steady intervals, but the edge (our HTTP->WS proxy) sometimes holds a 200–300ms aggregated buffer followed by a 20–30s gap of no socket writes before closing.
2) The connection close seen by the client sometimes maps to a proxy-side timeout (504) after the idle gap, not a backend failure.
3) There's a recurring pattern when response size > ~8k tokens and client is streaming in small-chunk mode.

Immediate mitigation I'm proposing:
- Reduce proxy output coalescing window to 150–200ms
- Enable TCP keepalive and application-level heartbeat every 10s on the edge for streaming routes
- Add temporary route for Bridgenet that bypasses intermediate cache layer (non-cached endpoint) while we monitor

I'll prepare a small config diff and push to canary edge for a quick test. If Sam can provide the example request id (and time) I can do a server-side replay to confirm fix.

Attaching initial pcap snippet analysis (see drive link).

—Dev
